newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks jump 116 pts, third biggest net gain.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks jump 116 pts, third biggest net gain.

text.p: Toronto stocks rallied more than 116 points on Thursday, the third-biggest net gain ever as Canada's largest equity market followed Wall Street higher.
The TSE 300 Composite Index soared 116.66 points to close at 5844.30 in brisk turnover of 108.8 million shares worth C$1.69 billion ($1.23 billion).
Advancing stocks overwhelmed declines 586 to 387 with 313 issues unchanged.
The TSE's performance was bettered by the Dow Jones Industrial Average which rocketed ahead 126 points on options-related buy programs and stronger bonds.
Canadian bonds enjoyed a strong session with the 9.00 percent benchmark bond up 1.90 to 110.45 to yield 7.117 percent.
Ira Katzin, an investment adviser with RBC Dominion Securities, said he expects equity markets to remain buoyant in the near term as Canadians begin to pour money into retirement savings investments.
"You put that together with the foreign investment coming into Canada and you have very strong demand for equities," Katzin said.
He added Friday is expected to be a volatile session due to triple witching -- the expiry of options, futures and options on futures -- in the United States.
Toronto's biggest sector gains were in financial services, consumer products, conglomerates and precious metals.
* Canadian Imperial Bank of Commerce was the top bank, closing up 2.15 at 57.95. Bank of Montreal gained 2 to 42.65.
* In golds, Bre-X Minerals Ltd. jumped 1.30 to 20.90 on 1.9 million shares. Bre-X is awaiting Indonesian approval for joint development of the Busang site with Barrick Gold Corp.
Barrick added 0.50 to close at 41.10 on 986,000 shares.
* Nickel miner Sherritt International topped the TSE's volume list, ending flat at 52 on 5.05 million shares.
* Methanex Corp. added 0.05 to 12.40 on 3.3 million shares.
